paragraphs.text: A cake of [Yunnan white tea](yunnan-white:definition) from Lincang. It is made from Yunnan's large leaf tea plants rather than the small bush cultivars of Fujian, where most [white tea](white:definition) is still made. White tea is the tea of fewest steps: the leaf is never heated to halt its change and never rolled, so it keeps its natural shape.

In Yunnan the leaf is [withered indoors or in shade](yunnan-white:making), out of the midday sun, then dried by air without the final low bake that Fujian white usually gets. Pressing it into a cake borrows one of the shapes of pu’er. Yunnan white is [new to the trade](yunnan-white:history), popular only in recent years, though local practice may be older.

brewing.text: Yunnan white is brewed gently, as a white tea is, in a gaiwan or small pot, and it gives many infusions; the leaf holds up well.

notice.text: A honeyed, sweet cup, often richer and fuller than Fujian white, with little bitterness, sometimes fruit like apricot or melon and a hay or herbal note. Yabao is sweet and silky, often with pine or herbal notes.
